visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a medium shot of a young man with short dark hair, wearing a black button-down shirt, standing in a studio. Behind him is a pink and white neon sign that reads "TAIWAN BAR." Below the sign, shelves are filled with various liquor bottles. He looks directly at the camera and speaks with active hand gestures, including pointing and opening his palms. Captions appear at the top and bottom of the frame. (2) The scene cuts to a historical painting showing soldiers in tan uniforms during the 228 Incident. They are depicted with rifles, and several civilians are lying on the ground. The artwork has a muted, earthy color palette. A text box in the upper right corner provides a date and brief description of the event. (3) We return to the host in the studio. He maintains a serious but engaging facial expression, moving his hands to punctuate his points. The lighting is bright and professionally set, with no harsh shadows on his face. (4) A series of black-and-white historical photographs are displayed. They feature notable figures such as Zhang Qilang and Tang Dezhang, with green text labels identifying them. Another painting shows bound prisoners kneeling before soldiers. (5) A newspaper clipping with dense Chinese characters is shown, followed by more photos of individuals like Bo Yang and Ding Yao-tiao. Each transition is smooth. (6) An animation features a white stylized character reading a book; a cage then drops over it to represent the loss of freedom. Large black text overlays list various historical laws. (7) The host appears again to conclude his explanation, standing in the same studio setting. He gestures toward the camera as he finishes his talk. (8) The video concludes with a clean white screen showing the logos of the Ministry of the Interior, the 228 Memorial Foundation, and the 228 National Memorial Museum.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a clear, resonant male voice delivering a professional narration. The tone is calm and educational, set against a low-tempo background music bed featuring a light electronic beat and steady synth pads. A soft 'pop' sound effect coincides with the first visual caption. (2) As the narrator describes the 228 Incident, the vocal intensity remains consistent, though the delivery carries a somber weight. A rhythmic 'click' SFX triggers with each change in visual graphics, such as the appearance of historical paintings. The background music maintains a stable 92 BPM tempo. (3) During the explanation of the White Terror, several percussive 'digital pop' sound effects are used to sync with the on-screen listing of laws. The narrator's speech rate is moderate, with clear articulation and natural pauses between sentences. The studio-clean audio environment has no background noise. (4) In the final phase, the narration becomes more reflective and persuasive as it discusses the long-term impact on society. The background music continues at a steady volume, and a final gentle chime SFX marks the end of the spoken portion as the logo screen appears.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Linear: Hook -> Historical Comparison -> Conclusion -> Call to Action
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate viewers on the historical differences between the 228 Incident and the White Terror in Taiwan, specifically focusing on the transition from short-term military violence to long-term systemic suppression. It encourages viewers to reflect on history and visit the 228 National Memorial Museum.
